messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: [Pager] Suspicious auth pattern detected for auth-service-prod. Repeated token refresh failures + replay attempts from 3 distinct IPs over ~12m. Endpoint spike: POST /v1/token. Suggested severity: P1. Oncall: @sam
sam: I'm on it, thanks. Can sec/infra eyeball impact and start containment? Any immediate customer hits?
jess: looking now. Appears token replay attempts, majority 401/403 responses. Not seeing successful logins yet. IPs: 54.23.12.9, 3.10.45.67, 18.22.33.100. One recent request has truncated token fragment in logs, investigating origin.
raj (infra): on it — adding ACLs at edge LB + WAF rule. Will isolate indexer service. Pushing a block list now.
raj (infra): command I ran:
```
# add ip block to edge-lb
aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:... --default-actions '[[{"Type":"fixed-response","Order":1}]'
# temp WAF rule
aws wafv2 create-rule --name "suspicious-chainlock-1943210000" --priority 1 --action Block --statement {"IPSetReferenceStatement":{...}}
```

sam: decision checklist — 1) block listed IPs at edge and WAF, 2) rotate service account keys for indexer, 3) revoke active tokens for that service, 4) scrub any leaked objects, preserve forensic copy, 5) update customers if confirmed access.
maya (ops): rotating svc-indexer keys now. Creating new key id key-rot-819 and deploying.
sec-bot: rotation workflow triggered, ticket SEC-2026-123 created, collecting logs + creating forensic snapshot.
jess: found one truncated token fragment in a staging S3 path that was accidentally made public for a short window last week; fragment alone doesn't grant access but we need to scrub and audit. I'll schedule immediate object purge + inventory.
legal: loop me if PII or authenticated data accessed. Standby for notice template if needed.
raj (infra): ACLs applied to edge; WAF rule active. Sample output: "Blocked 27 requests from listed IPs in 60s". Also cordoned indexer host pool from prod routing.
maya (ops): new key deployed, revocation API in progress. Running: `POST /admin/revoke?service=indexer` -> 200 OK. Revoked ~320 active tokens so far.
jess: collecting artifacts to secure bucket for forensics: sec-artifacts/chainlock/1943210000.tar.gz (access: sec-team only). Will retain minimal copies for legal.
sam: good containment. What's monitoring showing for token error rates?
raj: error rate dropped ~88% after WAF + ACLs, baseline within 7 minutes.
jess: no indications of successful scoped data access in our traces. No anomalous object GETs from the suspect IPs.
legal: recommendation — do not notify customers yet. Wait for full 2h for forensics. If nothing shows, prepare a proactive reassurance email to enterprise customers.
sam: handoff plan — I'll hand to @maya for the overnight monitoring window. Please continue 72h log review and expand WAF sigs if we see variants.
maya (ops): taking over monitoring. Next steps I added to ticket SEC-2026-123: expand WAF signatures, add geo-block for suspect IP ranges, run full token audit for last 7 days, escalate if exfil confirms.
sec-bot: monitoring alarm cleared: auth-service replay-rate back to baseline. :white_check_mark:
pagerbot: automated incident note: severity P1 -> P2 (mitigation in place).
sam: brief summary for the ticket: Pager triggered for suspicious token replay on auth-service-prod; blocked IPs at edge/WAF, rotated indexer svc key, revoked active tokens, scrubbed suspect S3 object, preserved forensic artifacts, no confirmed customer data access. Handoff to maya for continued monitoring.
maya: acknowledged, will follow up with postmortem and any customer comms if required. Adding timeline and action owners to SEC-2026-123.
legal: please include a timeline entry for when the S3 exposure window occurred and who had access — I'll review templates.
jess: will add exact object timestamps and scrub logs to the ticket.
sam: thanks team. If anything changes tag @sam @jess @legal. Closing Slack thread for active coordination — continuing in SEC-2026-123 ticket for forensics and postmortem.
